photo.title: Portrait of Chief Black Horn facing to the right, wearing a war bonnet and decorated skin shirt with recognisable hand motif. One of 16 black and white prints of the 'Oglala Sioux' [Lakota] arriving in London for the British Empire Exhibition at Olympia in 1925, mounted in an album scrapbook by Newton Turvey.

View of Chief Black Horn posed with a bow and arrow while crouching with W. M. Ghost Dog and his son, on the deck of a ship, with three people in the background, and a further person only half in the frame on the far right. One of 16 black and white prints of the Oglala Lakota [captioned 'Oglala Sioux'] arriving in London for the British Empire Exhibition at Olympia in 1925 mounted in an album scrapbook by Newton Turvey.

Group portrait of twelve people on board a ship, with eight individuals from the 'Oglala Sioux' [Lakota] Nation in the foreground caught in motion. One of 16 black and white prints of the Oglala Lakota [captioned 'Oglala Sioux'] arriving in London for the British Empire Exhibition at Olympia in 1925 mounted in an album scrapbook by Newton Turvey.

View of Chief Black Horn shaking hands with an American Navy captain, surrounded by Setting Spider, Henry Kills Enemy at Night, Sweetgrass, and two other unnamed (American?) men in the background. One of 16 black and white prints of the Oglala Lakota [captioned 'Oglala Sioux'] arriving in London for the British Empire Exhibition at Olympia in 1925 mounted in an album scrapbook by Newton Turvey.One of 16 black and white prints of the Oglala Lakota [captioned 'Oglala Sioux'] arriving in London for the British Empire Exhibition at Olympia in 1925 mounted in an album scrapbook by Newton Turvey.

View of Little Bull and Sweetgrass sat cross-legged smoking, with Setting Spider sat between them, lighting Sweetgrass's pipe.  One of 16 black and white prints of the Oglala Lakota [captioned 'Oglala Sioux'] arriving in London for the British Empire Exhibition at Olympia in 1925 mounted in an album scrapbook by Newton Turvey.

Portrait of a Dakota Oglala man named Tasunkakokipapi or Ta-shung-ga-ko-ke-pa (One Whose Horse Is Feared or Young Man Afraid of His Horses), wearing European clothing.  He is holding a feather fan and a cane.
Profile portrait of Tokeya Waci U Richardson, the great-great-great grandson of Sitting Bull.
Portrait of Michael Crandall Bissonette, great grandson of Chief Wa-Cha-Pe (Stabber), with fur cloak.

Full face, half length portrait of Red Shirt. (Ogalesha) [Main entry see B54.5e]
Full-face half length portrait of Red Shirt. Clothing European. Neck ornament of rows of dentalium shell. Hair, one braid and rest loose. '...has the finest suit of hair in his tribe'. Holding smoking pipe.

Portrait of Chief Black Horn holding the reins of horse near Waterloo Station. One of 16 black and white prints of the Oglala Lakota [captioned 'Oglala Sioux'] arriving in London for the British Empire Exhibition at Olympia in 1925 mounted in an album scrapbook by Newton Turvey.

Portrait of Chief Black Horn posed standing with a bow and arrow, facing to the right, with a wooden bench and tarpaulin in the background (possibly taken whilst onboard a ship). One of 16 black and white prints of the Oglala Lakota [captioned 'Oglala Sioux'] arriving in London for the British Empire Exhibition at Olympia in 1925 mounted in an album scrapbook by Newton Turvey.

Group portrait of eighteen individuals from the 'Oglala Sioux' [Lakota] Nation on board a ship. One of 16 black and white prints of the Oglala Lakota [captioned 'Oglala Sioux'] arriving in London for the British Empire Exhibition at Olympia in 1925 mounted in an album scrapbook by Newton Turvey.

View of eight Oglala Lakota [captioned 'Oglala Sioux'] individuals on horseback on a dirt ground, with crowds of people and building structures visible in the background. One of 16 black and white prints of the Oglala Lakota [captioned 'Oglala Sioux'] arriving in London for the British Empire Exhibition at Olympia in 1925 mounted in an album scrapbook by Newton Turvey.

View of eight men on horseback on Rotten Row in Hyde Park. One of 16 black and white prints of the Oglala Lakota [captioned 'Oglala Sioux'] arriving in London for the British Empire Exhibition at Olympia in 1925 mounted in an album scrapbook by Newton Turvey.

View of seven men sat cross-legged around a log fire, with two men (Little Bull and Setting Spider) holding pipes, and two further people (Ghost Bear and Mrs Ghost Bear) stood behind them. Two walls resembling a log cabin structure form the backdrop, with five horizontal posts extruding from the wall on the left, that each hold a set of horse tack. One of 16 black and white prints of the Oglala Lakota [captioned 'Oglala Sioux'] arriving in London for the British Empire Exhibition at Olympia in 1925 mounted in an album scrapbook by Newton Turvey.
Portrait of a Dakota Oglala man named A-san-pi (Milk), wearing a European shirt and vest.  His hair is adorned with an eagle feather and braids wrapped with fur.

Portrait of Chief Black Horn standing with arms folded in front of his chest, with the facade of a (London?) building in the background. One of 16 black and white prints of the Oglala Lakota [captioned 'Oglala Sioux'] arriving in London for the British Empire Exhibition at Olympia in 1925 mounted in an album scrapbook by Newton Turvey.

View of Chief Black Horn holding an axe with an American Navy captain, with Henry Kills Enemy at Night standing the other side of the captain, and four further people partially within view. One of 16 black and white prints of the Oglala Lakota [captioned 'Oglala Sioux'] arriving in London for the British Empire Exhibition at Olympia in 1925 mounted in an album scrapbook by Newton Turvey.

View of group of Oglala Lakota [captioned 'Oglala Sioux'] caught in motion while dancing on the deck of a ship, with about five onlookers in the background. One of 16 black and white prints of the 'Oglala Sioux' [Lakota] arriving in London for the British Empire Exhibition at Olympia in 1925 mounted in an album scrapbook by Newton Turvey.

View of group of five men stood drinking tea on the deck of a ship, with further people in the background and partially visible around the edges of the photograph. One of 16 black and white prints of the Oglala Lakota [captioned 'Oglala Sioux'] arriving in London for the British Empire Exhibition at Olympia in 1925 mounted in an album scrapbook by Newton Turvey.

View of Kills Enemy at Night and two other men painting a tipi in front of a backdrop painted with a European-style landscape scene. One of 16 black and white prints of the Oglala Lakota [captioned 'Oglala Sioux'] arriving in London for the British Empire Exhibition at Olympia in 1925 mounted in an album scrapbook by Newton Turvey.

Half length frontal portrait of Oglala man, Mi-Wa-Kan Yu-Ha-La (Sword), Captain of Native Police and Judge of Native Court 1875.  He wears European clothing, decorated with a watch fob chain and star shaped silver badge with his name on, and has braided hair.
